subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Sunk Cost Trap
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Sunk Cost Trap.

hook.text: You've already sent $5,000. The scammer asks for $2,000 more. You pay — because quitting means losing $5,000.

buildup.text: The sunk cost fallacy makes people continue investing in losses hoping to recover them.

discovery.text: Con artists deliberately create sunk costs early, knowing victims will chase their losses.

twist.text: Each additional payment deepens the commitment. The victim talks themselves into continuing.

climax.text: Casinos, scammers, and bad investments all exploit the same cognitive trap.

punchline.text: The money you already lost is exactly why you'll lose more.

quiz.question: What is the sunk cost fallacy?
options: Fear of missing out on deals
Continuing to invest because of what you've already lost
